tests/unit/test_structured_run.py:79-88 hits the restore+artifact branch via 'never any json' but asserts only `str(art) in str(ei.value)` and `pytest.raises(LLMRunnerError)` — no identity/subtype assertion, so the new preserve-identity-while-appending-path behavior is not pinned
advisory.finding: The new restore-and-append branch (StructuredOutputError restored from the cause chain AND artifact captured -> `restored.args` mutated, identical object re-raised) is never exercised with identity/subtype assertions. The happy-path identity test and the held-out restore tests all use default cfg with no `parse_failure_artifact_dir`, so `path` is always None and line 304 (`restored.args = (f"{restored} [raw reply captured: {path}]",)`) is untested for the property this diff adds. The only test that hits that branch (tests/unit/test_structured_run.py:75) predates the change, catches the broad `LLMRunnerError`, and asserts only that the artifact path substring appears in the message — it does not assert the re-raised error is the identical/typed StructuredOutputError. A regression that reconstructed a fresh UnretryableOutputError on the artifact path (discarding the original subtype/identity) would pass every test in the diff and the old substring assertion.
scenarios: Refactor or reversion that builds a fresh UnretryableOutputError when an artifact is captured, discarding the original StructuredOutputError subtype/identity
advisory.suggested_fix: In the held-out oracle, extend the sentinel identity test to set `cfg.parse_failure_artifact_dir = str(tmp_path)`, then assert `ei.value is sentinel`, `type(ei.value) is StructuredOutputError`, and that the captured artifact path appears in `str(ei.value)`.
